text_preview: RE: 48 bit graphics... A good reason (which is why many companies use it) for 48 bits / pixel is so you can use double buffering (for animating scenes) - i.e. you have 2 * 24-bit planes. You write to the one in the background, and then FLIP! -- the entire screen updates to the second image-plane. The screen updates in one refresh and you don't see different objects appearing in the order that they're drawn (as in the CAD/MacDraw effect). Now your ready to update the image that used to be in the foreground. Steve. ( <EMAIL> / iris.iit.edu) About the SG product line: who can even keep track nowadays?
